    • generatedNameWithSuffix

      public ClassName generatedNameWithSuffix(String suffix)
      Returns the name of a top-level type generated for this one, as processors name the code they generate for a type: in the same package, named after the simple names from the top-level type to this one, then a suffix, all joined by underscores. For com.example.Outer.Inner and the suffix Mapper, it is com.example.Outer_Inner_Mapper; for the top-level com.example.Outer, it is com.example.Outer_Mapper. generatedNameWithPrefix(String) puts the name of what the type is for first instead.

      Each type and suffix gets its own name. An underscore within a simple name or the suffix is written _0: an underscore followed by 0 is one of the type's, any other one joins two names, as no name starts with a digit. A_B.C gives A_0B_C_Mapper where A.B_C gives A_B_0C_Mapper, and A with the suffix B_Mapper gives A_B_0Mapper. Other characters, such as a dollar sign, are kept as they are. A type that is not generated can still have the name: whether a type has it already is for GeneratedSources.isAvailable(ClassName) to tell.

      Parameters:
      suffix - what the generated type is for this one, such as Mapper: a Java identifier, which may be a keyword
      Returns:
      the name of the generated type, without annotations
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the suffix is not an identifier: if it is empty, starts with a digit, or has a character that cannot be in an identifier, such as a dot or a space

    • generatedNameWithPrefix

      public ClassName generatedNameWithPrefix(String prefix)
      Returns the name of a top-level type generated for this one, with a prefix: in the same package, named after a prefix, then the simple names from the top-level type to this one, all joined by underscores. For com.example.Outer.Inner and the prefix Generated, it is com.example.Generated_Outer_Inner; for the top-level com.example.Outer, it is com.example.Generated_Outer.

      Underscores are written as generatedNameWithSuffix(String) writes them, so that each type and prefix gets its own name: A_B.C with the prefix P gives P_A_0B_C where A.B_C gives P_A_B_0C, and A with the prefix P_B gives P_0B_A.

      Both methods join the same way, so a name with a prefix is also the name of another type with a suffix when the prefix followed by the simple names of this type are the simple names of the other type followed by the suffix, and only then: Outer.Inner with the prefix Generated and Generated.Outer with the suffix Inner both give Generated_Outer_Inner, and so do Inner with the prefix Outer and Outer with the suffix Inner. Such a clash needs the prefix to be the simple name of a top-level type of the package, and the suffix that of a type of the package.

      Parameters:
      prefix - what the generated type is for this one, such as Generated or AutoValue: a Java identifier, which may be a keyword
      Returns:
      the name of the generated type, without annotations
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the prefix is not an identifier: if it is empty, starts with a digit, or has a character that cannot be in an identifier, such as a dot or a space
